claim_1.claim: GeneChip analysis of PBMCs from all vaccine recipients in the study on the day of the third vaccination and at 24 h and 72 h after vaccination, using Significance Analysis of Microarrays (SAM) with false discovery rate (FDR) <1% and z-score transformation across samples, showed that 63 unique genes from inflammatory response pathways were significantly up-regulated at 24 h after the third vaccination compared to the day of the third vaccination.

sources.quote: Figure 1 is a heat map showing the changes in expression of 63 genes associated with inflammatory responses on the day of the third vaccination and at 24 h and 72 h later. These genes are markedly up-regulated 24 h after vaccination; however, by 72 h after vaccination, they resolve to the levels of expression observed on the day of the third vaccination.

Figure 1. Strong but transitory changes in genes associated with inﬂammatory processes are associated with vaccination with adjuvanted RTS,S. Heat map of genes associated with inﬂammatory responses in all vaccine recipients in the study on the day of the third vaccination and at 24 h and 72 h after vaccination. Sixty-three unique genes from inﬂammatory response pathways are signiﬁcantly (false discovery rate [FDR], !1%) up-regulated 24 h after the third vaccination.

claim_7.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge, 39 volunteers who were vaccinated and then challenged, and 12 control nonvaccinated volunteers who were challenged, using principal components analysis of differentially expressed genes, showed 461 genes were up-regulated and 626 genes were down-regulated in 12 control nonvaccinated volunteers who were challenged compared to 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge.

sources.quote: We assessed global expression proﬁles from vaccine-naive per- sons, samples taken at day 5 after challenge of persons who had received vaccine and of persons who were challenged but had not received vaccine. The principal component analysis shown in Figure 2 shows 461 up-regulated genes and 626 down- regulated genes (identiﬁed at an FDR !1%) in persons chal- lenged and infected without vaccination.

Figure 2. The effect of vaccination and challenge on the global host response, as illustrated by principal components analysis of differentially expressed genes. Red spheres denote 36 RTS,S vaccine recipients at baseline before vaccination and challenge (group A). Blue spheres denote 39 volunteers who are vaccinated and then challenged (group B), and green spheres denote 12 control nonvaccinated volunteers who were challenged (group C). The separation of group A and group B reﬂects the combined effect of vaccination and challenge. The separation of group A and group C reﬂects the effects of challenge and challenge only. The separation of group B and group C indicates that volunteers who are vaccinated (group B) respond to challenge differently from those who are not vaccinated (group C).

claim_12.claim: GeneChip microarray analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at 2 weeks after the third vaccination before challenge, using high-resolution GSEA with running enrichment score and permutation testing, showed that the proteasome degradation pathway was up-regulated in the protected group compared to the nonprotected group.

sources.quote: Figure 4A shows the enrichment of genes in the proteasome degradation pathway that are up-regulated in persons in the protected group.
A, Running enrichment score (RES) showing that the proteasome degradation pathway is up-regulated in the protected group.

claim_13.claim: GeneChip microarray analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at 2 weeks after the third vaccination before challenge, using high-resolution GSEA with permutation testing and multiple-test correction, showed that the proteasome degradation pathway was the only gene set with both a significant nominal P value and an FDR less than 0.25 compared to the gene sets tested.

sources.quote: This was the only set of genes with both a signiﬁcant P value and a multiple test cor- rection FDR that was less than the default value of 0.25.

B, Permutation test of the signiﬁcance of the proteasome degradation pathway. The GSEA algorithm executes a permutation test to calculate the nominal P value and false discovery rate (FDR) of identiﬁed pathways. After multiple test correction, the FDR of the proteasome degradation pathway is 0.086, which is less than the default cutoff of 0.25.

claim_14.claim: GeneChip microarray analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at study entry, using GSEA, showed that no gene sets reached an FDR of less than 0.25 in the protected group compared to the nonprotected group.

claim_15.claim: GeneChip microarray analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at study entry, using GSEA, showed that the proteasome degradation pathway was not up-regulated in the protected group compared to the nonprotected group before vaccination.

sources.quote: indicating that the proteasome degradation pathway was not up- regulated in the protected group before vaccination.

claim_16.claim: Reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction analysis of PBMCs from 3 randomly chosen protected and nonprotected RTS,S vaccine recipients at 2 weeks after the third vaccination showed differential gene expression of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in the protected group compared to the nonprotected group.

sources.quote: Figure 6A shows reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain re- action conﬁrmation of differential gene expression in 3 ran- domly chosen samples obtained from protected and not pro- tected outcome groups at 2 weeks after the third vaccination and identiﬁed by expression data as genes associated with reg- ulation of MHC processing in the immunoproteasome path- way. Four pivotal genes were assessed.

claim_18.claim: qRT-PCR analysis of PBMCs from RTS,S vaccine recipients at 2 weeks after the third vaccination, using fold-change measurement relative to the sample with the lowest expression value for each gene and assay, showed that expression of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 was higher in protected subjects compared to nonprotected subjects.

sources.quote: Figure 6A shows reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain re- action conﬁrmation of differential gene expression in 3 ran- domly chosen samples obtained from protected and not pro- tected outcome groups at 2 weeks after the third vaccination and identiﬁed by expression data as genes associated with reg- ulation of MHC processing in the immunoproteasome path- way.

Figure 6. Reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) conﬁrmation of the up-regulation of PSME2, PSMA4, PSMB6, and PSMB9 in protected individuals. A, The fold change in gene expression (as shown on the y-axis) relative to the samples with the lowest expression value for a given gene and assay. Four genes (PSME2, PSMB9, PSMB6, and PSMA4) are displayed along the x-axis. Triangles and stars denote samples obtained from protected and nonprotected individuals, respectively. Fold change values denoted by triangles are consistently greater than those denoted by stars, conﬁrming the up-regulation of these genes in protected individuals.
